questions.subject: MICROECONOMICS
questions.topic: Budget line response to a price cut
questions.learningObjective: Identify budget line rotation after price cut
questions.stem: Note #201: when the price of X falls, the budget line pivots outward along which axis?

options.text: It pivots outward along the X-axis, expanding affordable X bundles.
It pivots outward along the Y-axis, expanding affordable Y bundles.
It shifts parallel outward, expanding both goods equally.
options.misconception: treats price cut as income increase

options.text: It pivots inward along the X-axis, shrinking affordable X.

questions.explanation: A price cut for X rotates the budget line outward along the X-axis. Parallel shift would require income change.

x=25 because half of income divided by price 2 gives 25.
x=12.5 because quarter of income divided by price.
x=20 because price times exponent gives 20.

questions.explanation: Cobb-Douglas spends fraction alpha on X: 0.5*100/2=25. Ignoring share doubles.

Substitution effect and income effect.

questions.stem: Note #205: explain compensating variation after a price increase.

questions.explanation: It measures income required to compensate for the price change. It differs from equivalent variation timing.

options.text: Demand is elastic throughout the price range.
Substitution effect alone drives quantity up with price.
The good is a luxury with positive income elasticity.
Strong income effect opposing and outweighing substitution effect.

questions.explanation: Giffen requires income effect to dominate substitution effect. Luxury or elastic demand does not suffice.

questions.explanation: Ordinal utility ranks bundles; monotonic transforms leave choices unchanged. Cardinal levels are unnecessary.

A luxury whose demand rises with income.
A good with zero income elasticity.
An inferior staple whose income effect outweighs substitution when price rises.

questions.explanation: Giffen is an inferior good with dominant income effect. Luxury or neutral goods are not Giffen.
